items.label: Chicken
items.blurb: The kitchen's blank canvas — thighs forgive, breasts demand precision; the skin is the prize.

items.label: Beef
items.blurb: From quick-seared steaks to collagen-rich braising cuts — match the cut to the clock.

items.label: Pork
items.blurb: The most versatile animal in the larder: belly for richness, shoulder for the braise, loin for speed.

items.label: Lamb
items.blurb: Grassy, sweet, faintly mineral — loves garlic, herbs, yogurt, and real fire.

items.label: Ground meat
items.blurb: Surface area is flavor: brown hard, season boldly, never crowd the pan.

items.label: Bacon
items.blurb: Smoke, salt, and fat in one strip — as much a seasoning as a food.

items.label: Sausage
items.blurb: Seasoned fat delivery system — the casing world from chorizo to andouille flavors everything it touches.

items.label: Duck
items.blurb: Rich dark meat under a fat cap built for crisping — render slowly, rest well.

items.label: Turkey
items.blurb: Lean and large — brining is not optional; the dark meat is the connoisseur's half.

items.label: Shrimp
items.blurb: Sweet, fast, unforgiving — the C-curl means done, the O means overdone.

items.label: White fish
items.blurb: The lean clan — cod to snapper — bright, delicate, cooked in minutes and ruined in seconds.

items.label: Salmon
items.blurb: Fatty enough to forgive, rich enough to cure, best pulled at just-blushing medium.

items.label: Tuna
items.blurb: Sear-rare or slow-confit — the middle ground is cat food; winter fish run fattest.

items.label: Crab
items.blurb: Sweet labor — buy it live or picked fresh; the brown meat is the flavor bank.

items.label: Lobster
items.blurb: Luxury that punishes overcooking — gentle heat, drawn butter, restraint.

items.label: Mussels/Clams
items.blurb: The self-saucing shellfish — their liquor is the dish; discard what won't open.

items.label: Squid/Octopus
items.blurb: Two minutes or two hours — nothing between; high heat flash or patient braise.

items.label: Scallops
items.blurb: Buy dry-packed, sear hard, one flip — caramel crust over sweet raw center.

items.label: Anchovy
items.blurb: The umami needle — melted into fat it disappears, leaving only depth behind.

items.label: Salt cod
items.blurb: The Atlantic's preserved backbone — soak well, then flake into fritters, stews, and brandade.

items.label: Tofu
items.blurb: A texture chameleon that carries any flavor — press it, marinate late, fry for skin.

items.label: Eggs
items.blurb: The most technical ingredient in the kitchen — binder, leavener, sauce, and supper.

items.label: Crawfish
items.blurb: Louisiana's spring crustacean — sweet tail meat born for boils, étouffée, and bisque.

items.label: Sardines
items.blurb: Cheap, oily, brilliant — grill whole in summer or lean on the tinned pantry year-round.

items.label: Ham/Prosciutto
items.blurb: The cured leg family — salty-sweet slices that season melons, pastas, and pizzas alike.

items.label: Smoked fish
items.blurb: Salmon to haddock — cure and smoke as seasoning; flake into chowders, pastas, and brunch.

items.label: Venison/Game
items.blurb: Lean, dark, iron-rich — needs added fat and fruit's sweetness; never past medium.

items.label: Liver & Offal
items.blurb: The strong register — soaked in milk, seared pink, or slow-simmered; iron and depth.

items.label: Onion
items.blurb: The kitchen's foundation stone — sweat for sweetness, caramelize for depth, raw for bite.

items.label: Garlic
items.blurb: Sharp when raw, sweet when roasted, bitter when burnt — the heat decides its voice.

items.label: Ginger
items.blurb: Warm citrus-heat — grated raw it bites, cooked it mellows into fragrance.

items.label: Scallion
items.blurb: Two ingredients in one stalk: whites for the pan, greens for the finish.

items.label: Shallot
items.blurb: The onion's refined cousin — sweeter, subtler, the base of every French vinaigrette.

items.label: Leek
items.blurb: Silk when braised, sweetness when sweated — wash between the layers, always.

items.label: Tomato
items.blurb: Summer's acid-sweet heart — never refrigerate; salt ten minutes before serving.

items.label: Potato
items.blurb: Starchy bakes and mashes, waxy salads and gratins — the variety is the recipe.

items.label: Sweet potato
items.blurb: Sugar disguised as a root — roast hard for caramel edges, mash with warm spices.

items.label: Carrot
items.blurb: Sweetness underground — raw crunch, roasted candy, or the aromatic base's quiet third.

items.label: Celery
items.blurb: The stealth aromatic — its salts season every stock; the leaves are free herbs.

items.label: Bell pepper
items.blurb: Sweet when ripe, grassy when green — char and peel for its silkiest self.

items.label: Chiles
items.blurb: Fire with flavor underneath — seed for less heat, toast for more depth.

items.label: Mushrooms
items.blurb: The umami vegetable — dry-sauté first, salt late, save every trimming for stock.

items.label: Spinach
items.blurb: Cooks down to nothing, carries everything — wilt in seconds, squeeze well for fillings.

items.label: Kale/Collards
items.blurb: The sturdy greens — massage raw, braise long, or crisp into chips; frost sweetens them.

items.label: Cabbage
items.blurb: Cheap, patient, transformable — slaw's crunch, kimchi's funk, the braise's silk.

items.label: Cauliflower
items.blurb: The blank-canvas brassica — roast to nutty edges, purée to silk, or steak it whole.

items.label: Broccoli
items.blurb: Trees for the char — high heat is its friend; the stems, peeled, are the sweet secret.

items.label: Zucchini
items.blurb: Mostly water, wholly willing — salt it first, cook it hard, or shave it raw.

items.label: Eggplant
items.blurb: A sponge for oil and smoke — salt, then roast or burn whole for its silkiest flesh.

items.label: Squash/Pumpkin
items.blurb: Winter's dense sweetness — roast hard; the caramelized edge is the dish.

items.label: Corn
items.blurb: Sugar racing the clock — eat fresh corn the day it's picked; simmer cobs into stock.

items.label: Peas
items.blurb: Spring's sweetness in a pod — frozen-at-field often beats traveled fresh; minutes, not hours.

items.label: Green beans
items.blurb: Snap and squeak — blanch bright or blister hard; the gray middle helps no one.

items.label: Okra
items.blurb: The Creole thickener — high dry heat kills the slime, long stews harness it.

items.label: Beets
items.blurb: Earth and sugar — roast in skins to concentrate; the greens are a second vegetable.

items.label: Cucumber
items.blurb: Cool water and crunch — salt to concentrate, smash for dressing to cling.

items.label: Lettuce/Greens
items.blurb: The fresh register — dress at the last second; cold, dry leaves hold vinaigrette best.

items.label: Avocado
items.blurb: Butter that grows on trees — ripeness is everything; acid guards the green.

items.label: Fennel
items.blurb: Anise in vegetable form — raw shaved it's bright; braised it turns sweet and silken.

items.label: Asparagus
items.blurb: Spring's six-week argument for seasonality — snap where it wants, cook barely.

items.label: Radish/Turnip
items.blurb: Peppery crunch raw, gentle sweetness cooked — butter and salt are the classic answer.

items.label: Plantain
items.blurb: The cooking banana — green for savory starch, black-ripe for caramel sweetness.

items.label: Olives
items.blurb: Bitter fruit made brilliant by brine — a salt source; season the dish accordingly.

items.label: Capers
items.blurb: Pickled flower buds — briny punctuation for fish, butter sauces, and anything rich.

items.label: Lemon
items.blurb: The kitchen's brightness dial — zest for perfume, juice for lift, always at the end.

items.label: Lime
items.blurb: Sharper, more floral than lemon — the acid of the tropics from tacos to tom yum.

items.label: Orange
items.blurb: Sweet citrus with a winter peak — zest into desserts, segment into salads, reduce into glazes.

items.label: Apple
items.blurb: Autumn's keeper — tart cookers collapse into sauce, crisp eaters hold in salads and tarts.

items.label: Banana
items.blurb: Sweetness by the degree of speckle — the riper, the better for batters and caramel.

items.label: Mango
items.blurb: The monsoon's gift — ripe for sweetness, green for sour crunch; two fruits in one.

items.label: Pineapple
items.blurb: Tropical acid-sweet with enzymes that tenderize — grill it, salsa it, upside-down it.

items.label: Berries
items.blurb: Fragile perfume — never wash until the moment; frozen is honest for cooking.

items.label: Coconut
items.blurb: Flesh, milk, and oil — the tropics' richness; toast the flakes, never boil the milk hard.

items.label: Dried fruit
items.blurb: Concentrated sweetness — plump in liquid before baking; the tagine's secret sugar.

items.label: Artichoke
items.blurb: The edible thistle — trim ruthlessly, lemon constantly; hearts reward the labor.

items.label: Parsnip
items.blurb: The carrot's sweeter winter cousin — frost-kissed and roasted, it's nearly dessert.

items.label: Celeriac
items.blurb: The ugly root with celery's soul — remoulade raw, silken in purées and gratins.

items.label: Tomatillo
items.blurb: The husk-wrapped tart engine of salsa verde — char or simmer, never skip.

items.label: Bean sprouts
items.blurb: Crunch and freshness by the handful — add at the last moment; heat wilts the point.

items.label: Arugula/Watercress
items.blurb: The peppery greens — dress lightly and let them argue with rich plates.

items.label: Pomegranate
items.blurb: Jeweled crunch and sour-sweet juice — autumn's garnish and the Levant's molasses.

items.label: Stone fruit
items.blurb: Peaches to cherries — high summer's brief perfume; grill the firm, eat the ripe over the sink.

items.label: Grapes
items.blurb: Beyond the fruit bowl — roasted alongside sausages or pickled, they earn a place in the pan.

items.label: Cilantro
items.blurb: Bright citrus-green (or soap, by genetics) — stems carry more flavor than leaves.

items.label: Parsley
items.blurb: The neutral brightener — when a dish needs 'something fresh,' this is usually it.

items.label: Basil
items.blurb: Sweet anise perfume that dies in heat — tear, don't chop; add at the very end.

items.label: Mint
items.blurb: Cooling lift for both lamb and dessert — bruise it for drinks, chiffonade for salads.

items.label: Dill
items.blurb: Grassy anise — the Nordic and Persian signature; loves fish, yogurt, and potatoes.

items.label: Thyme
items.blurb: The background herb — earthy hum that deepens stocks and braises without announcing itself.

items.label: Rosemary
items.blurb: Pine and resin — potent; one sprig seasons a whole roast, two argue with it.

items.label: Oregano
items.blurb: Pepper and punch — one of the few herbs stronger dried than fresh.

items.label: Sage
items.blurb: Musky and bold — brown butter's partner, stuffing's soul; fry leaves crisp for garnish.

items.label: Bay leaf
items.blurb: The quiet tea-nutmeg note in every long simmer — always in, always out before serving.

items.label: Lemongrass
items.blurb: Citrus perfume in a stalk — bruise and infuse, or mince the tender core fine.

items.label: Curry/Makrut leaves
items.blurb: Southeast Asia's aromatic leaves — bloom curry leaves in hot oil; tear makrut into soups.

items.label: Tarragon
items.blurb: French anise authority — béarnaise's soul; strong, so dose like a spice.

items.label: Chives
items.blurb: The gentlest allium — snip over eggs, potatoes, and cream at the finish.

items.label: Shiso
items.blurb: Japan's minty-basil leaf — wrap sashimi, fry in tempura, or chiffonade over rice.

items.label: Butter
items.blurb: The kitchen's luxury solvent — foam for basting, brown for nutty depth, cold cubes for sauce.

items.label: Milk
items.blurb: The gentle canvas — scald for custards, simmer for béchamel, never rush to a boil.

items.label: Cream
items.blurb: Richness that whips, mounts, and mellows — reduce it for sauce, chill it for peaks.

items.label: Yogurt
items.blurb: Tang plus tenderizing enzymes — the marinade of the subcontinent and the sauce of the Levant.

items.label: Sour cream/Crema
items.blurb: Cool tang that finishes — add off heat or it splits; crema drizzles where sour cream dollops.

items.label: Cheese (any)
items.blurb: The fermented milk universe — melt the young, grate the aged, crumble the brined.

items.label: Parmesan
items.blurb: Umami you can grate — the rind belongs in your next pot of soup.

items.label: Mozzarella
items.blurb: Milky stretch — fresh for salads, low-moisture for the melt; never the same job.

items.label: Feta
items.blurb: Brined sharpness — crumble over heat at the end; it softens but proudly refuses to melt.

items.label: Cheddar
items.blurb: From mild melt to crystalline age — sharpness is a spectrum; buy block, grate fresh.

items.label: Cream cheese
items.blurb: The soft tang of bagels and cheesecake — beat room-temperature or fight the lumps.

items.label: Coconut milk
items.blurb: The tropics' cream — don't shake the can when you want the thick top for frying curry paste.

items.label: Goat cheese
items.blurb: Bright lactic tang — fresh chèvre spreads and crumbles; ash-ripened logs earn the cheese board.

items.label: Blue cheese
items.blurb: Controlled mold, big voice — crumble against sweet, melt into butter for steaks.

items.label: Gruyère/Alpine
items.blurb: The melting aristocrats — nutty depth for fondue, gratins, and the only true croque.

items.label: Ricotta
items.blurb: Fresh curds, gentle sweetness — whip it smooth, bake it into fillings, dollop it warm.

items.label: Buttermilk
items.blurb: Acid in dairy form — tenderizes fried chicken, lifts pancakes, dresses ranch.

items.label: Rice
items.blurb: Half the world's staple — rinse for distinct grains, leave the starch for risotto's cream.

items.label: Pasta
items.blurb: Semolina engineering — salt the water like the sea, finish in the sauce, save that starchy water.

items.label: Noodles
items.blurb: The slurpable world — rice, wheat, and glass; each wants its own doneness and dressing.

items.label: Bread
items.blurb: Fresh for the table, stale for everything else — crumbs, panzanella, and pain perdu.

items.label: Flour
items.blurb: Protein decides the job — bread flour for chew, cake for tenderness, AP for the middle path.

items.label: Cornmeal/Polenta
items.blurb: Ground maize two ways — quick crust for frying, patient porridge stirred to silk.

items.label: Couscous/Bulgur
items.blurb: The quick grains of North Africa and the Levant — steam, fluff, and dress warm.

items.label: Oats
items.blurb: Breakfast and binder — toast first for nutty depth in both porridge and crumble.

items.label: Lentils
items.blurb: The no-soak legume — red ones melt into dal, green and black hold shape for salads.

items.label: Chickpeas
items.blurb: The versatile pulse — hummus silk, falafel crunch, and aquafaba's egg-white impression.

items.label: Black beans
items.blurb: Earthy and creamy — the Latin table's backbone; season the pot liquor well.

items.label: White beans
items.blurb: Butter-textured blank slates — cannellini to fava; their broth is the free soup.

items.label: Kidney/Pinto beans
items.blurb: The chili and refrito clan — always fully cooked; the simmer builds the sauce.

items.label: Semolina
items.blurb: Durum's golden middlings — pasta's backbone, gnocchi alla romana, and the crunch on roast potatoes.

items.label: Breadcrumbs/Panko
items.blurb: Crunch on demand — panko for shatter, fine crumbs for binding; toast before topping.

items.label: Phyllo/Puff pastry
items.blurb: Bought lamination is honest — thaw properly, work fast, butter between every phyllo layer.

items.label: Wrappers
items.blurb: Wonton to gyoza skins — the dumpling shortcut; keep covered, seal with water, pleat with pride.

items.label: Soy sauce
items.blurb: Fermented salt-umami — light seasons, dark colors; the wok's oldest friend.

items.label: Fish sauce
items.blurb: Liquid anchovies — a teaspoon deepens everything; smells loud, finishes invisible.

items.label: Oyster sauce
items.blurb: Sweet-savory gloss — the stir-fry's finishing lacquer and the vegetable's best friend.

items.label: Miso
items.blurb: Fermented soybean depth — white is sweet, red is loud; never boil the delicate ones.

items.label: Tahini
items.blurb: Sesame's butter — bitter-nutty silk for hummus, dressings, and secretly, cookies.

items.label: Peanut
items.blurb: Legume richness — satay's engine, the crunch on noodles, the butter in the sauce.

items.label: Sesame
items.blurb: Seeds and oil — toast the seeds, finish with the oil; heat murders its perfume.

items.label: Vinegar
items.blurb: The acid pantry — wine for vinaigrettes, rice for sushi, sherry for depth, balsamic for sweetness.

items.label: Wine
items.blurb: Cook only what you'd drink — reduce to lose the raw edge; it's structure, not decoration.

items.label: Beer/Cider
items.blurb: Fermented depth for batters, braises, and steamed mussels — bitterness concentrates, so choose gently.

items.label: Stock/Broth
items.blurb: Liquid foundation — homemade is banked flavor; store-bought improves with aromatics and a simmer.

items.label: Tomato paste
items.blurb: Concentrated summer — caramelize it in fat before liquid touches it; the brick-red moment matters.

items.label: Mustard
items.blurb: Acid-heat emulsifier — Dijon binds vinaigrettes, whole-grain adds pop, powder blooms in heat.

items.label: Mayonnaise
items.blurb: The cold emulsion — sauce base, sandwich law, and the secret to golden grilled cheese.

items.label: Honey
items.blurb: Floral sweetness with a season in every jar — it balances heat and glosses glazes.

items.label: Sugar
items.blurb: Sweetness and structure — caramel's raw material and savory cooking's quiet corrector.

items.label: Chocolate/Cocoa
items.blurb: Fermented, roasted complexity — bloom cocoa in hot liquid; save the good bars for eating.

items.label: Vanilla
items.blurb: Orchid perfume — real pods and pastes bloom in fat and cream; the world's favorite floral.

items.label: Nuts
items.blurb: Richness and crunch — always toast; raw nuts are a rough draft.

items.label: Tamarind
items.blurb: Sour-sweet pulp — pad thai's tang and the agrodolce of the tropics.

items.label: Curry paste
items.blurb: Aromatics pre-pounded — fry in coconut cream or oil until fragrant before anything else.

items.label: Pickles
items.blurb: Acid and crunch preserved — the palate's reset button; save the brine for dressings.

items.label: Seaweed/Nori
items.blurb: The ocean's greens — kombu builds dashi, nori wraps, wakame floats in soup.

items.label: Dried mushrooms
items.blurb: Concentrated forest — soak, then use both the caps and the strained liquor.

items.label: Kimchi
items.blurb: Korea's fermented fire — eat it fresh and crunchy or cook the sour old jar into stews.

items.label: Coffee/Espresso
items.blurb: Roast bitterness beyond the cup — deepens chocolate, rubs, and braises.

items.label: Maple syrup
items.blurb: The forest's caramel — grade B/dark for cooking; it glazes, sweetens, and balances heat.

items.label: Hot sauce
items.blurb: Fermented or fresh fire in a bottle — vinegar heat that seasons as much as it burns.

items.label: Cumin
items.blurb: Warm earth — the backbone of chili, curry, and the taco; toast whole, grind fresh.

items.label: Coriander seed
items.blurb: Citrus-floral warmth — cilantro's seed, nothing like its leaf; crush for brightness.

items.label: Paprika
items.blurb: Ground peppers from sweet to smoked — bloom in fat; pimentón brings the campfire.

items.label: Turmeric
items.blurb: Golden earth — color and quiet bitterness; blooms in fat, stains everything it loves.

items.label: Cinnamon
items.blurb: Warm bark — true Ceylon is delicate, cassia is bold; both bridge sweet and savory.

items.label: Cardamom
items.blurb: Floral-resinous pods — the world's third-priciest spice; crack before steeping.

items.label: Clove
items.blurb: Numbing warmth — powerful; count them in, count them out.

items.label: Star anise
items.blurb: Licorice architecture — pho's perfume and red-braising's signature; one star goes far.

items.label: Nutmeg
items.blurb: Warm and woozy — grate fresh over cream, greens, and béchamel; pre-ground is dust.

items.label: Saffron
items.blurb: The world's priciest harvest — bloom threads in warm liquid; there is no substitute.

items.label: Curry powder
items.blurb: The blend family — toast to wake it; garam masala finishes where curry powder begins.

items.label: Caraway
items.blurb: Rye bread's soul — earthy anise for cabbage, goulash, and the Central European table.

items.label: Allspice
items.blurb: One berry, three impressions — cinnamon-clove-nutmeg in a single grind; jerk's backbone.

items.label: Sumac/Za'atar
items.blurb: The Levant's tang — sumac is lemon in powder form; za'atar its herb-sesame blend.

items.label: Five-spice
items.blurb: China's warm licorice blend — star anise leads; rub it on duck and pork.

items.label: Old Bay/Creole
items.blurb: The Gulf and Chesapeake's house blends — celery salt, paprika, and attitude.

items.label: Sichuan peppercorn
items.blurb: Not heat but electricity — the numbing má that makes chiles dance; toast and grind fresh.
